items.headline: Josh Jacobs placed on the Commissioner's Exempt List, out indefinitely
items.summary: A league action, not an injury: he is paid but cannot practice or play, and there is no reinstatement date. It follows a May arrest reduced to two misdemeanours, with a court date reported for 17 November. A suspension on top of this is still possible, so the absence is UNKNOWN in length, not merely long.

items.headline: Green Bay's backfield is a committee created overnight: Lloyd, Brooks and a traded-for Kaleb Johnson
items.summary: Confirmed: Jacobs is off the roster and the Packers gave Pittsburgh a 2028 sixth-rounder for Kaleb Johnson the same day. Reported, not confirmed: who leads. Lloyd worked with the first team and is called a priority add, but he has a hamstring history; Brooks profiles as a third-down back. No three-down back is established, and the same-day trade reads as the team hedging its own depth chart.

items.headline: Zach Charbonnet moved to reserve/PUP: out a minimum of four games
items.summary: The four-game minimum is mechanical, not a projection — reserve/PUP at the cutdown deadline binds it. He is recovering from knee surgery reported as a torn ACL. He cannot be drafted as a Week 1 contributor.

items.headline: Nacua expected to avoid the exempt list and back at practice from the psoas issue
items.summary: Two separate things pushing the same way. Pelissero reports he is expected to avoid the Commissioner's Exempt List — reporting, not a league ruling, and Schefter noted on 30 August that the matter is still under review with no Week 1 deadline to decide. Separately he returned to practice from a psoas/groin problem and is not expected to miss the Melbourne opener.

items.headline: Jeanty still rehabbing an ankle sprain; his coach needs another week to judge Week 1
items.summary: Klint Kubiak said on the record that Jeanty is still on the mend. What is NOT established is severity — low or high sprain is undetermined, and that distinction decides everything. Sources disagree and the disagreement is kept: one outlet says there is a real chance he misses Week 1, another notes he is not on an injury report. Week 1 is genuinely UNKNOWN.

items.headline: Harbaugh calls it "reasonable to assume" Nabers plays the 13 September opener
items.summary: A coach quote plus an observable fact: Nabers shed the non-contact jersey and took live contact reps, his first since tearing an ACL and meniscus in Week 4 last year, with an April clean-up procedure after that. The remaining risk is a setback, not the current status.

items.headline: Rookie Jadarian Price is in line to lead Seattle's backfield for the first month
items.summary: Confirmed: Charbonnet is out at least four games and the remaining backs are Price, George Holani and Emanuel Wilson. Contested: Seattle's unofficial depth chart reportedly lists Holani ahead of Price, while analysts expect the 32nd overall pick to take the bulk of the work. Treat the lead role as likely, not settled.

items.headline: Saints place rookie WR Jordyn Tyson on IR: at least four games out
items.summary: Confirmed on 30 August as New Orleans cut to 53. The No. 8 overall pick has a recurring right-hamstring problem and one report puts the absence nearer two months, so the return date is a range and not a date. He misses at least the openers at Detroit and against Baltimore, Las Vegas and Atlanta.

New Orleans Saints place first-round pick on injured reserve

items.headline: Atlanta has not named a Week 1 starter between Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr.
items.summary: Reported by Schefter on 31 August: Penix is ramping up from the knee injury that ended his season and the team is still evaluating; Tagovailoa is healthy and started the preseason finale. No announcement. For a draft tonight this means every Atlanta pass-catcher carries an unresolved quarterback, which is a reason to discount Drake London and Kyle Pitts slightly, not to avoid them.

sources.title: Falcons news: Michael Penix Jr., Tua Tagovailoa plans revealed before Atlanta's starting QB announcement

items.headline: Dallas waived Jaydon Blue, and the backup job behind Javonte Williams changed twice in two days
items.summary: Confirmed: Blue — widely drafted as the Javonte Williams handcuff — was waived at the cutdown and went unclaimed. Malik Davis was the only other back to survive, then Dallas claimed Emari Demercado from Kansas City on Monday. Any cheat sheet still listing Blue as the Dallas handcuff is wrong, and the replacement is not settled either.

items.headline: Kittle activated off PUP with no setbacks, expected to take team reps this week
items.summary: He tore his right Achilles on 11 January. The activation and the no-setback reporting are credible-reporter facts; whether he plays the 11 September opener in Australia is still open. His price has risen roughly eight spots, which is the market pricing a risk rather than resolving it.

items.headline: Bowles is hopeful on Egbuka for Week 1, but the toe sprain leaves it unresolved
items.summary: His foot was rolled up in a 12 August joint practice and Bowles initially called him day-to-day, week-to-week. The coach's hope is a fact about what was said, not about availability. He should not be treated as a locked-in Week 1 starter, which matters tonight if your bench is thin.

items.headline: Rookie Mike Washington Jr. took first-team reps behind Jeanty and is the week's biggest riser
items.summary: Facts: he stepped into first-team work and produced in preseason, including a 53-yard run and 119 yards on 15 carries overall. Opinion, from an ADP column: a must-have backup in the double-digit rounds. His value is entirely derivative of Jeanty's ankle and evaporates if Jeanty is cleared.

items.headline: Jacksonville's own depth chart hedges on Tuten while its head coach endorses him
items.summary: Both halves are facts and they disagree. Tuten took the bulk of first-team reps after Travis Etienne left and Liam Coen said on the record he expects a big year — yet the initial unofficial depth chart lists Tuten and Chris Rodriguez as co-starters. One analyst shop has him on its avoid list at a top-60 price for exactly this reason.

items.headline: James Conner opens the season on IR: at least the first four games out
items.summary: Confirmed at the cutdown. He is still recovering from the ankle injury suffered in September 2025 and cannot return before Week 5 against Detroit. The wrinkle for Arizona: rookie Jeremiyah Love has a high-ankle sprain of his own, so Tyler Allgeier could carry a large Weeks 1-4 workload.

items.headline: Ja'Marr Chase hyperextended a knee in practice and is still expected to play Week 1
items.summary: It happened at practice on 25 August. He was limited on his return and is expected to play on 13 September against Tampa Bay. Nothing here changes his draft position, but it is the kind of item worth knowing before you spend a top-five pick.

sources.title: Every Player Suspended to Start the 2026 NFL Season

items.headline: Mahomes says he is on track to start Week 1 after December ACL surgery
items.summary: He said on 25 August that he has hit every rehab benchmark following surgery on 16 December for an ACL and LCL. The caveat that matters for fantasy is not availability but usage: his rushing upside is likely reduced, and that is where a chunk of his ceiling used to come from.

sources.title: Every Player Suspended to Start the 2026 NFL Season

items.headline: No prominent player is left in an unresolved holdout entering Week 1
items.summary: All four camp contract situations closed: Bijan Robinson signed a record running-back deal, Jahmyr Gibbs surpassed it two days later, Vita Vea extended and Tuli Tuipulotu is practising. Nothing here removes anyone from Week 1. The practical point is the reverse of a warning: do NOT apply a holdout discount to Robinson or Gibbs tonight, because those situations are closed rather than pending.

sources.title: Tracking 2026 NFL hold-ins: Vita Vea resolves contract situation

items.headline: Week 1 starts on Wednesday 9 September, and four teams lock before Saturday
items.summary: New England at Seattle opens the season on Wednesday 9 September, and San Francisco meets the Rams in Melbourne on Thursday 10 September — the Wednesday game exists to accommodate the Australia trip. The main slate is Sunday 13 September. If your league locks lineups at kickoff, players from SEA, NE, SF and LAR are unbenchable from midweek, which is a real cost on a fringe starter.

items.headline: Tyson's absence pushes Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele up the Saints' receiver order
items.summary: Confirmed: Tyson is out at least four games. Reported: Vele had been third in the rotation and moves up, and rookie Barion Brown survived cuts. The exact order behind Olave is not settled, but Olave's target share for the first month is the least ambiguous part.

sources.title: 4 Major Takeaways from the Saints Unofficial Depth Chart

items.headline: San Francisco puts Christian Kirk on IR and Isaac Guerendo on reserve/PUP
items.summary: Both confirmed at the cutdown. Kirk goes to IR with a designation to return for a calf strain; Guerendo to reserve/PUP with a torn pectoral, a mandatory four-game minimum. With Ricky Pearsall already out for the season, the receiver room thins and the back-up job behind McCaffrey is unresolved between Jordan James and rookie Kaelon Black.

items.headline: Romeo Doubs settles in as Drake Maye's WR2 behind A.J. Brown
items.summary: Facts: the Kayshon Boutte trade cleared the depth chart and Maye praised his route-running. The bull case is an environment bet and should be labelled as such — his former team ranked 30th in neutral passing rate, New England ninth. DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams are still in the room.

sources.title: Is Romeo Doubs a 2026 fantasy football breakout candidate?

items.headline: Jayden Higgins tore an ACL and is out for the whole season
items.summary: The injury happened in a joint practice on 18 August and was reported the next day. He was penciled in to start opposite Nico Collins, so the targets he would have taken move toward Jaylin Noel and Xavier Hutchinson — and Collins' own share firms up, which is a small point in his favour rather than against him. Out all 18 weeks.

items.headline: Alec Pierce activated off the active PUP list, targeting Week 1
items.summary: Activated on 27 August after a March clean-up on his left ankle and heel. The important structural detail: he avoided reserve/PUP, so he is NOT subject to a four-game absence. What remains uncertain is the practice ramp, not the eligibility.

sources.title: Colts Get Long-Awaited Alec Pierce Update Before Week 1

items.headline: Roschon Johnson is Chicago's back-up behind D'Andre Swift with Monangai week-to-week
items.summary: Monangai's MRI was clean but his coach called him week-to-week with a hyperextended knee and he is expected to miss the start of the season. The cut-day roundups name Johnson as the beneficiary. Swift's role as starter is unchanged — this only matters for the handcuff.

items.headline: Tank Dell placed on IR with a return designation, out at least four games
items.summary: He has not played since December 2024 after a multi-ligament knee injury, roughly 21 months. Week 5 is the earliest legal return date and not an expectation. Any 2026 role is speculative.

items.headline: Nick Chubb retired after eight seasons
items.summary: He announced it on the night of 21 August. Final and off every board — included only so nobody drafts him from a cheat sheet printed earlier in the month.

sources.title: Nick Chubb retires from the NFL

items.headline: Suspensions in force for Week 1: Jones (MIN) three games, Pearce (ATL) eight
items.summary: Jeshaun Jones is suspended the first three games under the substances policy, eligible again on 28 September. Atlanta's James Pearce Jr. is suspended eight games under the personal conduct policy, back on 2 November. Also serving: Nazeeh Johnson (TEN, six games), Phidarian Mathis (BUF, three) and Dorance Armstrong (WAS, one). None is a fantasy starter, but they are unavailable and a board that lists them is wrong.
